subject: Site-isolated architecture workshop — aligning calendars and pre-call asks
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@meditech.co>, Priya Shenoy <priya.shenoy@meditech.co>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next step: site-isolated architecture workshop (90m)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the discovery earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Summary of discovery: Meditech is evaluating a site-isolated (on-prem/VPC) deployment for patient-facing inference where PHI cannot traverse public shared tenancy. Key constraints: strict egress controls, no shared KV cache, and audit log retention for 7 years.
- Primary goals for the workshop: validate network/topology requirements, confirm identity/KMS flows, and walk through a candidate architecture (VPC peering vs. private link vs. air-gapped appliances).

Proposed next step: a 90-minute technical workshop with our ops & runtime architects to deep-dive on architecture and run through a short checklist. Suggested windows (PT):
  • Thu Apr 13 — 10:00–11:30
  • Fri Apr 14 — 13:00–14:30
  • Mon Apr 17 — 11:00–12:30

Please let us know which slot works best (or propose up to two alternatives). 

Pre-call asks (to help us prepare):
- Primary network contact and their firewall change window (so we can provide allowlist IPs).
- Whether you want us to use synthetic data or bring a small masked sample for latency checks.
- Any compliance docs you want our architects to have ahead of time.

I’ve attached a short checklist and a network access stub that will speed the workshop. We’ll follow up with an agenda once the time is locked.

Attachments: redwood-site-isolated-checklist.pdf (PDF stub), network-access-instructions.txt (text)

Thanks — looking forward to lining this up.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0112

Irene — thanks for the recap and the materials. Both useful.

We’d like to take Mon Apr 17 11:00–12:30 PT. That works for the core ops team here. A couple quick notes/questions before we lock: 
1) Attendees: please can you confirm who from Redwood will be on the call? We’ll bring our network lead (Priya) and an identity engineer.
2) Test data: we prefer you use synthetic data. If you need a small masked sample to exercise latencies, let us know and I’ll get approvals.
3) Timezone: we’re Pacific. Confirmed.

Once you confirm attendees I’ll send the invite from my calendar and include a dial-in.

Alex

Alex / Priya — great, thanks for picking the slot. Connor here (ops/runtime lead) — I’ll join the workshop along with Marissa (product). Quick notes from our side to make the session high-value: 

- Attendees from Redwood: Connor O'Brien (Runtime Architect), Marissa Cole (Product Ops), Irene Choi (Solutions Engineer).
- Proposed workshop flow (90m): 1) 15m high-level constraints review; 2) 35m topology + KMS/identity run-through; 3) 25m outage/failover & SLO discussion; 4) 15m actions and MAP.
- Network prep: If you can provide the bastion or NAT IPs we should be allowlisted, we’ll share our ephemeral origin IPs 48 hours before the call. If you have a maintenance window for firewall changes, please flag it.
- Security contact: please add your security engineer to the invite if possible so we can cover audit and retention questions live.

We’ll bring a short set of diagrams and a sample config. No production credentials will be exchanged.
